summary.text: The Great Barrier Reef, in the Coral Sea off Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system, with over 2,900 reefs stretching over 2,300 km.
Built by billions of tiny coral polyps, it is the world's biggest single structure made by living organisms and can be seen from outer space.
It faces pollution runoff, crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks and mass coral bleaching, and lost more than half its coral cover after 1985.

facts.label: Named by
facts.value: Matthew Flinders, after mapping it in 1802

items.prompt: The Great Barrier Reef is the biggest single structure made by living things. What built it?

options.label: Lava flows from undersea volcanoes
Billions of tiny coral polyps
Sand carried out by Queensland rivers
Shells of giant clams piled up

items.explain: The reef structure is composed of and built by billions of tiny organisms called coral polyps.

items.prompt: Coral reefs grew in the Coral Sea Basin, yet until about 25 million years ago northern Queensland could not support coral. Why?

options.label: The basin had not yet filled with seawater
Volcanoes kept the water too hot
It lay in temperate waters too cool for coral
Starfish ate every young coral that settled

items.explain: Northern Queensland was still in temperate waters south of the tropics, too cool for coral, until about 25 million years ago.

items.prompt: Why can't the reef's corals grow on a seafloor 200 metres down?

options.label: The pressure there crushes coral skeletons
The water there is far too warm
Too few fish live there to feed them
Too little sunlight reaches that depth

items.explain: Reefs grow only above a depth of 150 metres because of their need for sunlight.

items.prompt: In 2018 the number of baby corals born on the reef dropped sharply. What was behind this?

options.label: Many mature breeding corals died in 2016–17 bleaching
Tourists collected most of the coral eggs
Cold water that year slowed coral spawning
New fishing rules removed coral-eating fish

items.explain: Many of the mature breeding adults died in the 2016–17 bleaching events, which led to low coral birth rates.

items.prompt: A 2022 survey found the reef's greatest recovery in 36 years. What mainly drove it?

options.label: Divers replanting coral fragments by hand
A ban on all tourism across the reef
Regrowth of a fast-growing coral, Acropora
Removal of every crown-of-thorns starfish

items.explain: The recovery was mainly due to the fast-growing Acropora coral, the reef's dominant coral, regrowing across two-thirds of it.

items.prompt: Matthew Flinders used the term "barrier reef" for a particular kind of reef. Which kind?

options.label: Any reef that circles a lagoon far out at sea
Any reef that keeps ships or ocean waves off the coast
Any reef lying deeper than divers can reach
Any reef growing on top of a sunken volcano

items.explain: Flinders called any reef that kept sailing vessels or open-sea waves from reaching the coast a barrier reef.
